question: What type of germ causes most upper respiratory tract infections, like the common cold?
explanation: Spot on! Viruses (like rhinoviruses) are the culprits behind the vast majority of our everyday coughs and colds. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T3#GNS213_U2_T3_h1)

question: Which of these structures is part of the upper respiratory tract?
explanation: You got it! The upper tract includes the nose, sinuses, and pharynx, while tiny air sacs like alveoli are deep down in the lower tract. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T3#GNS213_U2_T3_h1)

question: What is the medical term for when the tonsils get inflamed and swollen?
explanation: Correct! Tonsillitis simply means your tonsils are inflamed and fighting off an infection. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T3#GNS213_U2_T3_h2)

question: A patient suddenly loses their voice and sounds very hoarse after a cold. Which part of the airway is likely inflamed?
explanation: Well done! The larynx is your voice box, so when it gets inflamed (laryngitis), your vocal cords swell and your voice gets raspy. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T3#GNS213_U2_T3_h2)

question: Which symptom is a classic sign of pharyngitis?
explanation: That's right! Pharyngitis is inflammation of the throat, making a painful, scratchy throat the main sign you'll hear patients complain about. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T3#GNS213_U2_T3_h3)

question: When a patient with a throat infection develops a high fever, tiredness, and swollen neck glands, what do these show?
explanation: Spot on! Fever and swollen lymph glands are signs that the whole body's immune system is active and fighting the germs. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T3#GNS213_U2_T3_h3)

question: What is the standard test used to check for a strep throat infection?
explanation: Correct! A quick swab of the back of the throat helps us check if streptococcus bacteria are causing the trouble. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T3#GNS213_U2_T3_h4)

question: Why don't doctors do throat swabs for every person who walks in with a mild cold?

options.A: Most common colds are viral and resolve with supportive care
options.B: Laboratory tests are completely inaccurate for respiratory illnesses
options.C: Testing always causes severe physical trauma to the throat
options.D: Viral infections require immediate intravenous antibiotics

explanation: Exactly! Since normal colds are viral and clear up on their own, testing and antibiotics aren't needed—just rest and fluids. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T3#GNS213_U2_T3_h4)

question: Why should a nurse explain to a patient that antibiotics won't cure a regular viral cold?

options.B: Viral infections always require surgical drainage
options.C: Viruses do not respond to antibacterial drugs

explanation: You got it! Antibiotics only kill bacteria, so taking them for a virus won't help you feel better any faster. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T3#GNS213_U2_T3_h5)

question: What important advice should you give a patient given a 10-day course of antibiotics for strep throat?

options.A: Crush the tablets and mix them with cold fruit juice
options.B: Finish all the pills even if you feel completely better
options.C: Stop taking the medication as soon as your sore throat stops
options.D: Double the next dose if you miss a single pill

explanation: Spot on! Always encourage patients to finish every single pill. Stopping early can let the strongest bacteria bounce back and cause drug resistance. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T3#GNS213_U2_T3_h5)

question: What is the absolute top nursing priority when caring for someone with a severe upper airway problem?
explanation: Correct! Airway is always number one in nursing. If they can't breathe well, nothing else matters as much. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T3#GNS213_U2_T3_h6)

question: A toddler with a throat infection starts making a harsh, high-pitched breathing sound (stridor) and flaring their nose. What should you do right away?

options.A: Encourage the child to eat a large solid meal
options.B: Notify the healthcare provider and prepare for airway support
options.C: Discharge the child home with instructions to rest
options.D: Apply a tight nasal pack to stop the secretions

explanation: Great clinical judgment! Stridor and nasal flaring mean the airway is struggling or narrowing. Call the doctor immediately and get ready to help the child breathe. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T3#GNS213_U2_T3_h6)

question: Which of these is a BAD habit when trying to stop the spread of a respiratory infection?

options.A: Coughing into the inside of your elbow
options.B: Proper disposal of used paper tissues
options.C: Frequent hand washing with soap and water

explanation: You got it! Sharing cups or spoons transfers saliva and germs straight to others, spreading the infection around. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T3#GNS213_U2_T3_h7)

question: Why is it so important to treat strep throat quickly with antibiotics?

options.A: To ensure the patient never catches another cold ever again
options.B: To permanently shrink the size of the palatine tonsils
options.C: To cure viral rhinitis and clear nasal congestion instantly
options.D: To prevent serious systemic complications like rheumatic fever

explanation: Spot on! Early treatment stops strep bacteria from travelling around the body and causing serious issues like rheumatic heart disease. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T3#GNS213_U2_T3_h7)
